absent: Handler selection logic and supported name prefixes behind virtual attribute resolution.
Write permission predicate for program driven attribute mutation.
Layout and capacity rules of the resizable destination used by program read helpers.
Concrete attribute storage and mutation implementations of owning filesystems.
Lifetime and ownership rules for dentries, inodes and kernfs nodes beyond local uses.
Hash parameters and concurrency rules of the simple attribute cache beyond single lookup.
Socket attribute backend and its persistence scope.
Full registration and attachment semantics of the BPF helper set beyond the shown filter.
Folio, mapping, block plug and bio submission internals.
Integrity information lifecycle and verification algorithm.
Sticky error semantics of address space error recording.

findings.text: The filesystem exposes virtual set and remove operations for extended attributes that reject POSIX access control names, resolve a handler for the owning inode, require that the handler provides a mutation operation, and delegate the request to that operation. An empty set is treated as a present empty value rather than deletion, while removal is encoded as a mutation with absent value and zero length plus replace semantics.

Privileged programs may mutate dentry attributes through locked and unlocked entry points. The unlocked forms validate that the dentry has an inode, serialize with the inode lock, and forward to the locked form. The locked removal form checks write permission, invokes virtual removal with the initial identity mapping, and emits an attribute change notification on success.

Tracing programs may read user namespace attributes from control groups and sockets and may resolve the effective data inode behind a file. The read helpers accept a name and a resizable destination, enforce namespace restriction, validate destination usability, and forward to the respective subsystem getter. The inode helper resolves stacking to the underlying data object.

The block buffer layer exposes completion callbacks for synchronous and asynchronous reads and writes plus helpers to submit a buffer and to write a dirty buffer. Completions translate device status into cache validity, record errors, release the buffer lock, and when appropriate complete the enclosing folio operation. Dirty writes are skipped when the dirty marker was already cleared.

Metadata buffers can be associated with an address space through an initializer and a synchronizer. Initialization prepares a lock, an empty queue and the owning mapping. Synchronization writes dirty associated buffers, waits for in flight work, preserves still dirty entries on the owner, and reports failure when any waited buffer loses validity.

Kernel filesystem nodes expose attribute retrieval that consults optional per node attributes and a shared cache. When no attribute storage exists the lookup reports absence. Otherwise the request is served from a hash indexed by owning list and name, with size negotiation between caller buffer and stored value.
Virtual attribute mutation never handles POSIX access control names; such names are rejected with operation not supported before handler resolution.
A set with zero length is normalized to an empty present value and must not be interpreted as removal. Removal is distinct and uses an absent value with zero length and replace semantics.
Program accessible reads of control group and socket attributes are limited to the user namespace; other namespaces are denied with a permission error regardless of storage contents.
Newly allocated per node attribute storage starts with an empty attribute list, root ownership, synchronized timestamps taken from real time, and zeroed usage counters.
Inspection of dirty and writeback state over the buffers of a folio requires the folio lock to be held; a folio without attached buffers yields negative results for both outputs.

Attribute fetch returns the stored length when only length is requested, copies the value when the destination is large enough, reports range error when the destination is too small, and reports absence when no table or no entry exists.

Resolution of the effective dentry returns the stacking operation result when the dentry advertises a real operation, otherwise the dentry itself. Data inode resolution applies this rule with the data type and then derives the inode.

Integrity verification is attempted only for folios within the file size and only when integrity is active for the inode and the device read succeeded. One build always reports inactive and provides no info, while the active build checks a flag with ordering guarantees.

The buffer list of a folio is stored in its private field, and the offset of a buffer within its page is derived from its data address masked by page size. Touching a buffer marks its folio as recently used.

Concurrent creation of per node attributes uses compare exchange so that only one allocation becomes visible; losers discard their allocation and observe the winner. A non allocating lookup never creates storage.
Mutation of dentry attributes from programs serializes on the owning inode lock held across the entire locked operation, with release always performed before returning the status.

Buffer exclusive access uses a lock bit with uninterruptible input output wait for acquisition and a clear plus wakeup for release. A separate wait primitive sleeps for the same bit without acquiring ownership.

Asynchronous completion coordinates sibling buffers through an interrupt safe spinlock anchored in the first buffer of the folio. Flag clearing, buffer unlock and sibling scan occur under this lock to elect a single completer.

Association queue membership is protected by the owner lock, with assertion that direct removal holds it. Detachment from an unknown owner uses read side critical section pinning plus opportunistic locking and revalidation to tolerate migration. Synchronization holds the owner lock while draining and requeues under the same lock.

Root lookup, hash lookup and metadata error recording execute under read side protection without blocking. Slow block lookup uses the folio lock in blocking context and the mapping private lock in atomic context, and bails when migration is flagged.

Deferred verification carries a work item, a buffer reference and integrity context. The work handler validates the folio range covered by the buffer and then completes the asynchronous read with the validation outcome before freeing the carrier.

Per node attribute storage links an attribute list, ownership identifiers, three timestamps and usage counters for count and total size. Counters start at zero and the list starts empty under read copy update initialization.

Each buffer links into at most one metadata owner queue through a list node and a back pointer to the owner. Conversion from queue node to buffer uses container linkage, and emptiness of the owner list indicates absence of associated buffers.

A buffer moves from locked to unlocked on every completion, with validity set on success and cleared on failure. Asynchronous paths additionally clear their async marker under lock and only the last sibling to clear triggers folio completion. Dirty is cleared atomically at submit time.

Asynchronous reads normally complete directly, but when integrity info exists the buffer is handed to a work queue for validation and completion is deferred until validation finishes. Failure to allocate the handoff forces immediate completion as invalid.

Program access to filesystem helpers depends on program type and registration state. Unknown identifiers pass through, privileged monitor type is always allowed, non operation types are denied, configuration phase without operations passes, and otherwise only non mutating helpers are allowed for the misc operation.

Slow block resolution derives a page index from block number and block size, acquires the folio, rejects entries under migration, scans the circular buffer ring for a mapped match, and distinguishes fully mapped misses that warn from partially unmapped cases that stay silent.

Metadata synchronization proceeds in two phases: a plug assisted drain that detaches candidates, rewrites dirty entries and requeues busy ones to a temporary queue, followed by a wait phase that reattaches still dirty buffers to the owner and accumulates failure from invalidated waits.

Filesystem helpers are published as a kernel module owned identifier set with a custom filter, registered at initialization for monitor programs and conditionally for operation programs when the misc feature is enabled.

Device completions enter through per operation callbacks that unwrap the buffer from the request, propagate quiet marking, release the request, and dispatch to synchronous or asynchronous buffer finalization.
Successful attribute removal from programs emits a filesystem attribute change notification against the affected dentry.
The program driven removal path deliberately omits the post removal security hook after success because reentering the same helper from the hook could deadlock.

Concurrent completions of sibling buffers could both conclude the folio is finished; the design requires holding the uptodate lock across flag clearing and sibling inspection to ensure a single folio completion. Similar care applies to dirty checks versus requeue in metadata sync.

Write failures are recorded both on the buffer and stickily on the folio mapping and current metadata owner, while read failures only affect validity. Quiet marking suppresses error logging and is inherited from the originating request.

Racing creators of attribute storage must handle installation failure by observing the winner rather than leaking or double installing. Slow block lookup must not return buffers from folios flagged for migration.

Facts: removal is encoded as a set with absent value, zero length and replace flag; POSIX control names yield operation not supported; missing attribute storage or entries yield no data; short destinations yield range error; absent inode yields invalid argument; disallowed namespace yields permission error; failed waits yield input output error.

Facts: file release helper carries release semantics; dentry get, file get, dentry set, dentry remove and data inode helpers carry sleepable semantics with the data inode additionally nullable; socket read carries read copy update semantics when networking is enabled; only dentry set and remove are restricted to monitor programs.
